summary: Source-anchored research for Timestamp APIs (oldest/stable/pinned). Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: WiredTiger timestamps express application time, separate from internal transaction IDs. They are unsigned 64-bit values; API configuration strings encode them in hexadecimal without a leading 0x. (high confidence)

Alibaba Cloud's MongoDB 4.0 source analysis independently connects slow oldest-timestamp advancement with excessive version retention and cache pressure. Its memory-residency details describe the 2018 implementation. (medium confidence)

WT-4715 documents a historical cache-stall investigation involving an eviction participant pinning old transaction state. Its reported reproducer explicitly disabled timestamps, so it does not establish a timestamp-specific failure. (low confidence)

The development checkpoint guide describes checkpoint_timestamp as saved stable_timestamp metadata rather than the checkpoint transaction's read timestamp; startup recovery removes updates newer than that boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

WiredTiger timestamps represent application time rather than necessarily wall-clock time. They operate alongside internal transaction IDs; timestamped reads must also satisfy snapshot visibility. (high confidence)

Percona's March 2023 recovery experiment records distinct recovery and oldest timestamps, and checkpoint output carries oldest and checkpoint timestamps separately. These logs illustrate observable boundaries rather than a single database timestamp. (low confidence)
oldest_timestamp declares the earliest timestamp for future reads. Advancing it permits discarding earlier history, but existing readers at earlier timestamps remain protected. (high confidence)
query_timestamp(get=pinned) reports the minimum of oldest_timestamp and active reader timestamps, including a running checkpoint. It is read-only and can lag oldest_timestamp. (high confidence)

Applications manage oldest_timestamp and stable_timestamp through WT_CONNECTION::set_timestamp. Normally oldest must not exceed stable, and neither moves backward; forcing backward movement can expose incomplete history and inconsistent results. (high confidence)
Advancing stable_timestamp alone neither starts a checkpoint nor changes data durability. The newly eligible updates become recoverable through a subsequent checkpoint. (high confidence)

In their 2022 WiredTiger protocol model, Ouyang et al. make an update visible only if it passes transaction-ID snapshot checks and has a non-null timestamp no later than the transaction's read timestamp; the model encodes both tests in one visibility predicate. (high confidence)
roundup_timestamps=(read=true) on WT_SESSION::begin_transaction raises a requested read timestamp below oldest to oldest; it leaves a later read timestamp unchanged. (high confidence)

The 11.0 timestamp guide scopes rollback_to_stable to checkpoint-durable data: logged tables and untimestamped updates are unaffected. It requires resolved transactions, reset or closed cursors, and no concurrent API calls. (high confidence)

query_timestamp exposes oldest_reader, last_checkpoint, and recovery separately from oldest_timestamp and pinned. These distinguish active-reader retention, the last checkpoint boundary, and the boundary recovered at startup. (low confidence)

WT_CONNECTION::set_timestamp sets oldest_timestamp and stable_timestamp. WT_CONNECTION::query_timestamp retrieves global state using selectors such as get=pinned, get=oldest_timestamp, get=stable_timestamp, and get=oldest_reader; pinned is read-only. (high confidence)

For checkpoint-durable tables, stable_timestamp bounds the updates included in timestamped checkpoints. The saved checkpoint timestamp supplies the recovery boundary; use_timestamp=false explicitly overrides timestamp filtering. (high confidence)

Failing to advance oldest and stable as writes accumulate can retain history and increase cache pressure. Alibaba Cloud's MongoDB 4.0 explanation independently emphasizes timely advancement of both boundaries. (high confidence)
